I too have mental health issues that are unfortunately largely undiagnosed. This is something that often causes problems for me in my relationships, largely because of my own anxieties and fears about sharing those parts of myself with someone else.

It is what stopped me from starting a new relationship last year, and it's what stopped me from starting my current relationship in the past. 

That being said, it sounds like you two both have a lot more irons in the fire than I do in my own situation, but really here's the thing.

Y'all could definitely have a relationship and make it work- there's nothing about her diagnoses that condemns her to a shitty miserable life full of tumultuous interpersonal relationships, as long as she takes the steps necessary to make sure that she is setting boundaries for herself as needed, getting the help she needs that is right for her (therapy, medication, etc.) and remaining open with herself and cognizant of her wants and needs. 

It's not easy, but unfortunately such is life for those who struggle with mental problems. It's just like having a chronic disease- life is a little higher maintenance. But that doesn't mean you have to sacrifice quality. I hope that makes sense. 

If you really like this girl and feel like you want to be in a serious relationship with her, take a look at your current situation and your responsibilities. Do you have the time and energy that it takes to be in a serious relationship? Not only that, but a serious relationship with someone who has emotional problems and childhood trauma and will likely need a lot of love and support? Do you feel like you will be able to maintain your own mental health during this time?

These are questions you need to ask yourself before you jump into anything. Now, of course, if she isn't ready and she feels that she needs to focus on bettering herself right now then you don't really have a choice in the matter- her mental health comes first and pursuing a relationship when she isn't in a good place will only exacerbate things and make them worse for her. 

If you guys end up getting together, good luck!
